previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with multiple myeloma, end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, chronic hemolytic anemia, and dementia, was admitted after an unwitnessed fall resulting in a left intertrochanteric femur fracture. He underwent left hip hemiarthroplasty and was managed postoperatively for hospital-acquired pneumonia, likely aspiration-related, which presented with fevers and worsening lung infiltrates. He completed a 5-day course of broad-spectrum antibiotics followed by a 7-day course due to persistent fevers, after which he remained afebrile. He also experienced acute toxic-metabolic encephalopathy, which improved over time. His kidney function and hemoglobin stabilized, and he participated in physical therapy. He was discharged to extended care rehab with a plan for wound care, aspiration precautions, dialysis, and follow-up with orthopedics and oncology.
problems: Pathological fracture in neoplastic disease, left femur, initial encounter for fracture
Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food and vomit
Enterocolitis due to Clostridium difficile, not specified as recurrent
Unspecified dementia, unspecified severity, without behavioral disturbance, psychotic disturbance, mood disturbance, and anxiety

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multiple myeloma, AMS, bilateral leg

abscess/mets.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal imaging was performed with T2, T1, and IDEAL technique,
followed by axial T2 imaging. This was followed by sagittal and axial T1
images obtained after the uneventful intravenous administration of ___ 
contrast agent.

COMPARISON:  MRI lumbar spine dated ___ and ___.

FINDINGS: 

Examination is mildly degraded by motion.

In keeping with the prior report, there is transitional anatomy with
lumbarization of the S1 segment.  There is unchanged grade 1 anterolisthesis
of L5 on S1.  Redemonstration of anterior compression deformities of T11
through L4, similar to prior exam.  Schmorl's nodes are again identified at
T12, L 2, and L5 endplates.

There is diffusely heterogeneous marrow signal abnormalities throughout the
visualized lumbar spine compatible with clinical history of multiple myeloma. 
There is no definite evidence of abnormal contrast enhancement.

The visualized spinal cord is normal in caliber and configuration with no
evidence of edema.  The conus medullaris terminates at the level of L1-L2.

Multilevel multifactorial degenerative disc disease of the lumbar spine is
similar to prior exam as detailed in the prior report.  There is moderate
spinal canal narrowing at L2-L3 and mild-to-moderate spinal canal narrowing
from L3-L4 through S1-S2.  There is moderate bilateral neural foraminal
narrowing at L5-S1.

Other: Incompletely evaluated nonenhancing T2 hyperintense lesions in the
right kidney statistically likely represent cysts.

IMPRESSION:


1. Diffusely heterogeneous bone marrow signal abnormalities of the lumbar
spine compatible with clinical history of multiple myeloma.
2. No evidence of spinal cord signal abnormality enhancement.
3. No evidence of epidural fluid collection.
4. Multilevel multifactorial degenerative disc disease of the lumbar spine,
most pronounced at L2-L3 with moderate spinal canal narrowing.
5. Moderate bilateral neural foraminal narrowing at L5-S1.

EXAMINATION:  BILAT LOWER EXT VEINS

INDICATION:  ___ year old man with multiple myeloma, ESRD on HD, recent hip
surgery has been immobile, now with persistent tachycardia and low grade
temps.// Please evaluate for DVT iso persistent tachycardia.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale, color, and spectral Doppler evaluation was performed
on the bilateral lower extremity veins.

COMPARISON:  Left upper extremity ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS: 

There is normal compressibility, flow, and augmentation of the bilateral
common femoral, femoral, and popliteal veins. Normal color flow and
compressibility are demonstrated in the bilateral posterior tibial and right
peroneal veins.  The left peroneal veins are not well seen.

There is normal respiratory variation in the common femoral veins bilaterally.

No evidence of medial popliteal fossa (___) cyst.

IMPRESSION:


1. Limited evaluation of the left peroneal veins.
2. Otherwise, no evidence of deep venous thrombosis in the right or left lower
extremity veins.

conjunction with the Speech-Language Pathologist from the Voice, Speech &

FINDINGS: 

Penetration with both thin and nectar thick liquids the does not clear from

IMPRESSION: 

Penetration with thin and nectar thick liquids.  However, no overt aspiration
seen.

Please note that a detailed description of dynamic swallowing as well as a
summative assessment and recommendations are reported separately in a
standalone note by the Speech-Language Pathologist (OMR, Notes, Rehabilitation
